metadata.intro: Welcome to the Mathematical Methods in Physics gateway. This roadmap connects the foundational tools of calculus and linear algebra to the advanced geometry and group theory that form the language of modern physics.

pillars.title: 1. Calculus, Vector Analysis & Differential Equations
pillars.narrative: The foundational tools for describing continuous change, gradients, and boundary value problems in physical space.

pillars.title: 2. Linear Algebra & Matrix Theory
pillars.narrative: The mathematics of state spaces, linear operators, and unitary transformations required for quantum mechanics and flavor physics.

pillars.title: 3. Complex Analysis & Integral Transforms
pillars.narrative: The power of analytic continuation, contour integration, and integral transforms for solving physical systems and scattering amplitudes.

pillars.title: 4. Group Theory & Symmetries
pillars.narrative: The algebraic study of invariance, providing the structural foundation for the Standard Model and conservation laws.

pillars.title: 5. Differential Geometry & Topology
pillars.narrative: The advanced mathematics of curved manifolds, forms, and invariants essential for General Relativity and modern condensed matter.

pillars.title: 6. Special Functions, Asymptotics & Variational Calculus
pillars.narrative: Orthogonal polynomial eigenfunctions, saddle-point and WKB asymptotics, functional derivatives, causal Laplace-Kramers-Kronig dispersion, and stochastic Fokker-Planck dynamics.

pillars.title: 7. Distributions, Integral Equations & Geometric Physics
pillars.narrative: Schwartz generalized functions, Fredholm and Volterra integral operators, multiple-scale singular perturbations, symplectic Hamiltonian manifolds, and principal fiber-bundle gauge geometry.

pillars.title: 8. Topology, Spinors & Computational Physics
pillars.narrative: Homotopy classification of topological defects, Clifford algebras and spinor representations, Monte Carlo Metropolis-Hastings sampling, spectral and finite-element PDE discretizations, and tensor-network matrix product states.

pillars.title: 9. Experimental Methods, Signal Processing & Detectors
pillars.narrative: Multivariate error propagation and chi-squared/maximum-likelihood estimation, Bayesian inference and model selection in physics, signal processing with power spectral densities and matched filtering, particle detector Bethe-Bloch energy loss and electromagnetic calorimetry, and cryogenic dilution refrigeration with scanning probe microscopy.
